discovery: Development of next-generation (massively parallel sequencing-by-synthesis) DNA sequencing technology
rationale: Recent prizes went to MOFs (2025), protein design (2024) and quantum dots (2023). That leaves room for a chemistry-to-life-sciences prize, a pattern the committee often follows. Solexa/Illumina sequencing-by-synthesis rests on chemistry: reversible-terminator nucleotides, fluorescent labeling and surface cluster amplification. It changed genomics and medicine, and its inventors have already won major prizes (Breakthrough Prize 2022, Millennium Technology Prize 2020), which often come before a Nobel. Controlled radical polymerization (Matyjaszewski, Sawamoto, Rizzardo) is a strong alternative.
